item.content:encoded:
A group of 18 new U.S. Peace Corps volunteers will serve in Tonga for two years following the completion of an intensive ten-week PreService Training program.

The group were sworn-in during a ceremony on Friday, 28 August, at Siva’s Café in Te’ekiu. Deputy PM Hon. Dr Viliami Latu, formally accepted the 18 new volunteers on behalf of the Tonga government, welcoming their commitment to serve communities across the Kingdom.

“Peace Corps Volunteers have served in the Kingdom of Tonga since 1968 and since then more than 1,700 Americans have served here. We are grateful to the Tongan government for their unwavering support of the Peace Corps program and our Volunteers,” said Peace Corps’ Country Director for Tonga, Elizabeth Neason.

The cohort of 18 trainees arrived in June from 13 different U.S. states, united in their commitment to serve the people of Tonga. Throughout the training period, the trainees dedicated themselves to personal growth, cultural learning, and technical preparation. Their program included approximately 150 hours of Tongan language and culture, 50 hours of health, safety, and security training, and 140 hours of specialized education, and environment sector preparation. Hosted by families in Te'ekiu, Ha'utu, and Fahefa, the trainees immersed themselves in Tongan daily life and customs, strengthening crosscultural understanding and forming strong community relationships. They also participated in practicums that placed them directly into classrooms and communities, allowing them to apply their teaching techniques and environmental education skills in realworld settings.

Seven volunteers will serve in education, teaching English language skills to primary and middle school students, collaborate with teachers, and support community literacy efforts.

Eleven trainees will serve in the environment sector, partnering with local organizations to promote environmental stewardship, strengthen naturebased resilience practices, and support disaster preparedness and risk reduction initiatives.

Peace Corps Tonga ackowledged the host families, training staff, ministry and NGO partners, and the medical and administrative teams, for their guidance and support.

The Ministers of Education, Agriculture, and Fisheries, members of the diplomatic corps, NGO s, host families, and Peace Corps staff joined the ceremony.
